title: Developer Launchpad: technical anchors & pricing lines
body:
Purpose:
This working brief bundles technical anchors, three candidate quickstarts, and a set of compact pricing and microcopy options for the Hosted API landing + onboarding flows. Audience: engineers evaluating integration (first 5–60 minutes), developer advocates building sample apps, and PMs iterating on copy for the sign-up/console experience.

High-level developer-first thesis (one line):
Give builders immediate wins: a tiny frictionless integration, measurable latency/cost expectations, and a clear upgrade path when they need scale or isolation.

Core value props (developer-centric, short bullets):
- Integrate in minutes: single-API key, one endpoint for text/chat/embeddings, pre-baked SDKs for JS/Python, and a runnable example that returns streaming tokens in < 5 lines.
- Predictable performance: published p50/p95/p99 latency profiles for each model; per-request region selection and automatic fallback to compatible variants if capacity is constrained.
- Cost clarity & control: tokens billed with transparent unit prices, SDK helpers for batching and KV-cache hints, and free test credits that reveal expected monthly unit costs for your traffic sample.
- Production-ready from day one: built-in retries, per-route quotas, and canary rollouts that let you start in hosted mode and move to Dedicated/Private without rewriting code.

Technical anchors to cite on pages and in emails (short, verifiable claims):
- Average cold-start overhead for hosted short-chat requests: ~35–70ms (depends on model family).
- Typical p95 token generation latency for standard text prompts (32–128 tokens): 80–220ms on curated models.
- SDK snippet ready to stream tokens in 3 lines (JS/Python).
- Auto-batching reduces per-token cost by up to 2–3x for high-throughput workloads; default heuristic enabled in SDK but opt-out available.
- KV/prefix cache reduces repeated prompt costs by retaining embeddings and token-state for deterministic flows.
(Operational note: these numbers are example anchors for marketing; engineering must sign off before publishing.)

Competitive angle (short memo):
- Direct competitors: LLM API providers that emphasize convenience but obscure performance numbers. Counter: publish transparent performance memos and show route-by-route latency histograms in the Console.
- Cloud providers: offer generic endpoint hosting but not inference-optimized kernels. Counter: highlight model/runtime co-design and tuned kernels we run for each model family.
- Self-hosted runtimes: appeal to teams that want control. Counter: emphasize onboarding speed + clear migration to Dedicated/Private when they need it.

Three candidate quickstarts (developer journeys with copy + technical checkpoints):
1) Hello Streaming (30s -> 5 minutes)
  - Goal: show token streaming and function/tool calling in a tiny example.
  - Landing copy: "Get a streaming chat response in under a minute — copy, paste, run."
  - Steps: npm install @redwood/infer; paste example; run playwright or curl to see token stream.
  - Technical checkpoints: show how to enable region selection, show p95 latency for this model on the sample page, present estimated cost for a single run.
  - Progression CTA: "Pin this model to a route" -> adds per-route quota and analytics.

2) Embed & Search: Local Product Recommendations (5–20 minutes)
  - Goal: integrate embeddings to power a simple Q/A over product docs.
  - Landing copy: "Add semantic search to your app with three API calls."
  - Steps: small script to create embeddings, store in a vector index (customer-managed or hosted), run a similarity query, and call generate() with context.
  - Technical checkpoints: show per-call cost estimate; show how batching embeddings saves cost; provide a preset model and quantization advice for inference cost savings.
  - Progression CTA: "Upgrade to Dedicated for predictable throughput" with link to capacity calculator.

3) Canary to Dedicated (10–60 minutes config + ramp)
  - Goal: show how a team can start in Hosted, run a canary, and then reserve Dedicated capacity without code changes.
  - Landing copy: "Start hosted, commit capacity as you grow — same API, lower unit cost at scale."
  - Steps: deploy a canary route (UI wizard), configure rollout % and fallback model, observe traffic in Console, commit to Dedicated via a guided flow.
  - Technical checkpoints: show cost delta table (hosted vs reserved) for common QPS/latency targets; include timeline for provisioning Dedicated hardware.

Pricing-language drafts (tone: transparent, engineer-friendly):
- Headline: "Pay for what you use, control how fast and cheap it gets."
- Starter line: "Free trial credits, pay-as-you-go tokens, and predictable reserved plans when you commit."
- Core thoughts to keep: list unit cost clearly (per 1k tokens or per embedding), link to cost calculator, show example bill for a sample app (e.g., 10k monthly short-chat requests = $X).
- Upsell path: "Reserve Dedicated capacity for a predictable lower per-token rate and guaranteed p99 SLAs."
- Refund/credits policy line: "Unused trial credits expire after 90 days; committed capacity is billed monthly with flexible scaling options."

Microcopy examples (short snippets for CTA, banner, email):
- CTA (signup): "Try Hosted — 3000 free tokens" or "Start free: run a streaming example now"
- In-console tip: "Enable auto-batching to lower cost for bursts"
- Billing banner: "Estimate your monthly token cost — try the calculator"
- Upgrade modal: "Reserve Dedicated capacity to reduce unit costs and add SLA"
- Email subject (dev): "Run a streaming example in 60 seconds (free credits inside)"

Developer FAQ (short):
Q: How do I estimate cost for my workload?
A: Use the in-console estimator (paste sample traffic) or run the cost-sampler CLI that replays a small batch of representative requests and reports projected monthly spend.

Q: Can I pin a model to a route?
A: Yes. Routes let you lock model version, set quotas, and observe token-level costs per route.

Q: What happens on capacity limits?
A: Smart routing falls back to compatible model variants and automatically retries where appropriate; your app will receive clear HTTP response metadata to detect fallback.

Sample landing hero paragraph (developer tone):
"Redwood Hosted API: a single, predictable API for streaming chat, embeddings, and structured outputs. Get a demo up in minutes, see exact latency and cost numbers for your sample traffic, and grow seamlessly from hosted to dedicated capacity."

Open questions for review with Eng/Product before publishing:
- Lock the exact latency anchors by model family (p50/p95/p99) and confirm wording for ‘cold start’ vs ‘steady-state’.
- Approve default limits and free credits amount for the Starter experience.
- Finalize the phrasing around Dedicated provisioning time and refund/commit terms.

Next steps / owner actions:
- Eng: validate the sample p95/p99 numbers and provide a small CSV of latency profiles per model (Marcus).
- Docs: add the three quickstart scripts to docs/quickstarts and create a short screencast (Elena).
- GTM: pick hero microcopy and run A/B test for CTA text (Sofia).

Notes: keep drafts intentionally concise and technical — this is targeted at developers who want numbers and runnable examples, not long marketing narratives.

End of brief.
